title: Deciding on your first team member
moduleTitle: Shared: Growing and managing a team
audience: Owners of small Australian property trade businesses who are considering their first hire or subcontractor
learningOutcomes: Decide whether the business is ready to hire, using repeat demand, cash and workload evidence.
Decide between an employee and an independent contractor using the working arrangement, not the label.
Screen and interview a candidate using skills checks, references and a check of any licence claim.

instruction.heading: Confirming the business is ready
instruction.body: Hiring is often the step that makes a small business feel fragile. Before hiring, check the evidence: repeat work and steady enquiries, a cash buffer that covers wages and on-costs for several months, and admin and job records showing that the extra capacity is needed. The milestone plan in “Milestone planning: six months, one year and five years” is the place to write the hiring trigger. A hire made because the owner is busy for one month often becomes a loss when the work drops away.

instruction.heading: Choosing the working relationship
instruction.body: Decide whether the person will be an employee or an independent contractor. The label in a contract does not decide the relationship. The way the work is done, who controls it, who supplies the tools, and whether the person works for others all matter. Employment obligations, including minimum pay under the applicable award or agreement, leave, superannuation, workers compensation and payroll tax, must be checked before any offer is made. Confirm them with the Fair Work Ombudsman or a registered employment adviser.

instruction.heading: Screening for skills and reliability
instruction.body: Set the skills the role needs, and test them. A practical task or a short site test shows more than a résumé. Check references from people who have seen the candidate work, and check any licence or certificate the candidate claims to hold on the state or territory register. Ask how the candidate handles a job that goes wrong, how they communicate with clients, and how they plan their day. Trust matters, because the person will enter client homes and represent the business.

instruction.heading: Taking care with friends and family
instruction.body: Hiring someone you know can work, but the relationship can make it hard to give direction, correct errors or end the arrangement. If you hire someone close to you, agree the role, the hours, the pay and the expectations in writing, and treat the arrangement as a work relationship. Where the budget allows, hire for a skill the owner does not have, because that adds capacity rather than copying the owner's skills. Look for someone who finishes tasks without constant direction.

procedure: Check the hiring trigger from the milestone plan, the repeat work evidence and the cash buffer before deciding to hire.
Decide whether the role is an employee or a contractor, by assessing the working arrangement and the obligations for each.
Write the role description, with the skills, licences and tasks needed.
Test skills with a practical task, and check references and licence claims on the register.
Agree the terms, pay, hours and start date in writing before the first job.
Schedule a review after the first month, and record what worked.

workedExamples.situation: One candidate is an experienced plasterer who holds a licence for plastering work in the owner's state. A second candidate is a general labourer with no licence. The owner needs help with patching and with general cleanup.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Which candidate fits the first role, and what must be checked before any offer?
workedExamples.reasoning: The plasterer may carry out licensed plastering work only within the licence category, and the owner must check that licence on the state register before making an offer. The labourer can support cleanup and general tasks, but cannot do licensed work.

equipmentAndPpe: Role description with skills, tasks and licence needs
Practical task sheet for the skills test

commonErrors.error: Hiring because the business is busy this month, without a cash buffer.
commonErrors.prevention: Hire on a trigger from the milestone plan, with a cash buffer covering several months of wages and on-costs.

commonErrors.error: Calling someone a contractor to avoid obligations.
commonErrors.prevention: Assess the relationship from how the work is actually done, and check the obligations before the offer.

commonErrors.error: Accepting a licence claim without checking the register.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the state or territory register, and keep the record with the date checked.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Confirm each one with the relevant authority or a registered adviser before hiring.

A worker doing licensed work must hold the licence for that work in the state or territory where the work is done. Using an unlicensed person for licensed work does not make the work lawful. This lesson does not grant any licence.

qualityStandard: The hiring decision names the trigger from the milestone plan, and the cash buffer that covers it.
The working relationship is assessed from the actual arrangement, and the obligations are recorded.
Each candidate's skills and licence evidence are checked on the register, with the date.
documentationEvidence: Hiring trigger and cash buffer record
Role description and skills test record
Written terms of engagement and the reference check record
summary: Hire on evidence: repeat demand, a cash buffer and a clear trigger.
Decide employee or contractor from the working arrangement, and check the obligations.
Test skills and check licence evidence before making an offer.

knowledgeChecks.question: What should be true before an owner hires a first team member?
options: The owner is busy this month and the diary is full for the next six months and the owner has no help
A hiring trigger from the milestone plan, repeat demand, and a cash buffer covering wages and on-costs
A friend has asked for the job and the friend has offered to work for half the usual rate on the job
The owner has bought a van and the van has a large cargo area, new paint and a roof rack

knowledgeChecks.question: How is the employee or contractor question usually decided?
options: By the label written in the contract and the wording of the contract and the label on the first page of the form
By the working arrangement: who controls the work, who supplies the tools, and whether the person works for others
By whichever option the contractor's preferred form lists first and the tax form the contractor files
By the candidate's choice alone and what the candidate would like to be called in the team and on the website

knowledgeChecks.question: A candidate says they hold a licence for licensed work. What should the owner do?
options: Accept the claim, because it was stated and the candidate seems honest, keen and very well qualified
Check the licence on the state or territory register, and keep the record with the date
Ask the candidate's friend to confirm it and the friend's own licence number
Let the candidate do the work and check later once the job has been finished
